title: Perfect core in a separable closure
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] of characteristic $p>0$, let $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ be a separable closure of $K$ [def-pd-separable-closure], and put $K_{\mathrm{perf}}=\bigcap_{n\ge0}\{a^{p^n}:a\in K\}$. Let $S$ be the subfield of $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ consisting of the elements separable algebraic over $K_{\mathrm{perf}}$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]. Then $S=\bigcap_{n\ge0}\{a^{p^n}:a\in K^{\mathrm{sep}}\}$.

proof.text: Write $C=K_{\mathrm{perf}}$ and $D=\bigcap_{n\geq0}(K^{\mathrm{sep}})^{p^n}$. Frobenius is an injective field homomorphism, so every power image is a subfield and so are $C,D$. The field $C$ is perfect: given $c\in C$, choose $b\in K$ with $b^p=c$. For every $n$, choose $u\in K$ with $u^{p^{n+1}}=c$. Then $(u^{p^n})^p=b^p$, and injectivity gives $b=u^{p^n}$. Thus $b\in C$ and Frobenius on $C$ is surjective.

source.place: Exposé IV, Lemma 3.2.2, proof, printed p. 56 (PDF p. 62): coefficientwise Frobenius of the minimal polynomial.

proof.text: By the relative-separable-closure definition, $S/C$ is algebraic. Since $C$ is perfect by Step 1, the algebraic-extension perfectness theorem makes $S$ perfect. For $s\in S$, recursively take $p$th roots in $S$, obtaining for every $n$ an element $s_n\in S$ with $s_n^{p^n}=s$. As $S\subseteq K^{\mathrm{sep}}$, this gives $s\in D$ and hence $S\subseteq D$.

source.place: Exposé IV, Lemma 3.2.2, proof, printed p. 56 (PDF p. 62): coefficientwise Frobenius of the minimal polynomial.

proof.text: Conversely, let $x\in D$, and for each $n\geq0$ choose $x_n\in K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ with $x_n^{p^n}=x$. Every $x_n$ is separable algebraic over $K$, since $K^{\mathrm{sep}}/K$ is separable algebraic. Let $f$ be the monic minimal polynomial of $x$ over $K$, and $f_n$ that of $x_n$. Apply the iterated-Frobenius minimal-polynomial identity with $F=K$, $E=K^{\mathrm{sep}}$, $a=x_n$. It gives $f(T)=\sum_i b_{n,i}^{p^n}T^i$ when $f_n(T)=\sum_i b_{n,i}T^i$. Thus for each coefficient $c_i$ of $f$ and every $n$, $c_i=b_{n,i}^{p^n}\in K^{p^n}$; hence every $c_i$ lies in $C$. In particular $f\in C[T]$, it is monic of positive degree, and $f(x)=0$.

source.place: Exposé IV, Lemma 3.2.2, proof, printed p. 56 (PDF p. 62): coefficientwise Frobenius of the minimal polynomial.

proof.text: The polynomial $f\in C[T]$ is irreducible: a factorization into two positive-degree polynomials over $C$ would give the same factorization over $K$, contradicting its minimal-polynomial irreducibility. It is therefore the minimal polynomial of $x$ over $C$. Moreover $f$ is separable over $K$, so its derivative is nonzero; the same derivative computed over $C$ is nonzero since $C\hookrightarrow K$ is injective. Any nonconstant common divisor of $f,f'$ in $C[T]$ would, by irreducibility of $f$, be associated to $f$, impossible since $\deg(f')<\deg f$. The Euclidean algorithm thus gives $Uf+Vf'=1$ in $C[T]$. This is separability over $C$. Consequently $x$ is separable algebraic over $C$, so $x\in S$ by its defining membership condition. This proves $D\subseteq S$ and the equality.
